route.title: Vision and Reported Embassy Overture
route.marker: The vision label, Lord-says formula, first-plural report, envoy notice, and embedded plural summons all occur in verse 1; verse 2 begins a direct first-person verdict against the addressed 'you'.
route.rationale: Obadiah 1:1 forms a layered overture that identifies the vision, reports news, names an embassy, and voices the international summons before direct Edom address begins.
route.rejected: Joining 1:1-4 would preserve the continuous oracle but hide the report-to-direct-address seam; treating the English quotation punctuation as exact Hebrew scope would overstate the witness.
route.basis: A complete vision/report/messenger speech act closes within verse 1, while the following behold-clause changes discourse level and person.
route.counter: Hebrew lacks an explicit quotation introducer at the exact WEB punctuation point, and the summons conceptually initiates the judgment developed through 1:4.
route.guard: Mandatory 1:1-9 hydration; quotation scope, antecedent, authorship, date, Jeremiah direction, and nation identity remain unresolved.

route.title: Pride in the Heights Brought Down
route.marker: The first-person verdict 'I have made you small' opens direct address; heart-pride, rock-height, internal boast, eagle/star comparison, and 'I will bring you down' reach a speech-formula close at 1:4.
route.rationale: The announced abasement is explained by the addressee's elevated self-security and answered by a matching descent verdict, producing a complete charge-to-judgment oracle.
route.rejected: Separating 1:2 from 1:3-4 would detach verdict from its pride rationale and answer; extending through 1:5 would cross into new thief and grape-gatherer comparisons.
route.basis: Second-person address, a quoted heart-question, concessive height clauses, and the final divine descent answer create a tightly closed oracle.
route.counter: Verse 2 is syntactically complete, and the entire address remains the outworking of the international summons in verse 1.
route.guard: The pride and height imagery cannot authorize national stereotyping, modern identity claims, or a generalized proof text detached from 1:1-9.

route.title: Plunder, Betrayal, and the Collapse of Wisdom and Might
route.marker: Paired thief and grape-gatherer questions open at 1:5; ransacking, allied betrayal, failed understanding, destruction of wisdom, and Teman's warrior dismay progress to total cutoff at 1:9.
route.rationale: The comparisons establish how ordinary thieves leave a remainder, then the oracle intensifies through exhaustive plunder, treacherous allies, lost understanding, and military collapse.
route.rejected: Splitting 1:5-7 from 1:8-9 honors the renewed divine formula, but verse 7's failed understanding is directly resumed by the loss of wisdom and warriors; isolating 1:5 turns a rhetorical comparison into a proverb.
route.basis: Rhetorical questions, an emphatic ransacking answer, allied deception, and the wisdom-to-warrior sequence form one escalating dismantling movement.
route.counter: The speech formula at 1:8 and the shift from plunder/betrayal to wisdom and military defeat create a real internal submovement.
route.guard: Jeremiah 49 overlap is undirected form evidence only; difficult ally/bread wording, source direction, event, and collective identity remain undecided.

route.title: Brother-Violence and the Calamity-Day Chain
route.marker: The causal brother-violence charge opens at 1:10; standing aloof on the day and repeated 'do not' plus 'in the day' clauses accumulate through the final prohibition against handing over survivors at 1:14.
route.rationale: Verse 10 states the forensic cause, verse 11 narrates participation by inaction, and verses 12-14 expand it into a cumulative calamity-day prohibition chain.
route.rejected: Isolating 1:10 creates a portable accusation, while splitting 1:10-11 from 1:12-14 separates the summary charge and narrated scene from the behaviors that specify them.
route.basis: Causal syntax, repeated day language, anaphoric negatives, escalating actions at gate and crossroads, and the fugitive-delivery climax yield a single indictment.
route.counter: Verse 10 is a complete shame-and-cutoff verdict, and verse 11 shifts into retrospective scene description before the negative-command series.
route.guard: Hydrate 1:10-16; do not lock the chain to one historical event, inherited guilt, modern Edom identity, or a universal retaliation ethic.

route.title: The Day upon All Nations and Proportional Reversal
route.marker: 'For the day of Yahweh is near upon all nations' expands the horizon; as-you-did recompense and the paired drinking comparison carry the reversal through disappearance at 1:16.
route.rationale: The day formula generalizes the preceding charge, then reciprocal deed language and an as-so drinking image complete one proportional reversal declaration.
route.rejected: Keeping 1:10-16 as the only child preserves causality but hides the all-nations reset; splitting 1:15 from 1:16 detaches the image that develops the announced recompense.
route.basis: Paired causal and comparative constructions link nearness, return upon the doer's head, drinking, swallowing, and disappearance.
route.counter: The initial 'for' depends on the accusation chain, and each verse can read as a formally complete declaration with different imagery.
route.guard: No day chronology, fulfillment scheme, historical event, drinking antecedent, or judgment ethic may be decided by this seam.

route.title: Zion Deliverance, House Reversal, Possession, and Kingdom
route.marker: The adversative Mount Zion turn opens deliverance, holiness, and possession; house-fire reversal, repeated possession forms, territorial register, ascent/judgment, and 'the kingdom will be Yahweh's' close the book.
route.rationale: Repeated Zion, house, possession, Esau, and kingdom language bind the five-verse coda, but the speech seal at 1:18 and register opening at 1:19 create a genuine unresolved retrieval choice.
route.rejected: Surfacing 1:17-18 and 1:19-21 could honor the fire-oracle close and possession-register opening, while the literary 1:17-18, 1:19-20, 1:21 route recognizes the final acclamation; both risk detaching dependent children from the complete coda.
route.basis: The Zion counterturn initiates possession, the house reversal supplies its conflict image, verses 19-20 realize possession geographically, and verse 21 returns to Zion for the kingdom climax.
route.counter: The divine speech seal at 1:18 is a strong close, verse 19 begins a distinct register, and verse 21 changes from place enumeration to climactic acclamation.
route.guard: Never expose 1:21 alone; no option may decide territorial entitlement, modern mapping, identity, violence ethics, messianic/ecclesial fulfillment, witness, or later-reuse authority.
route.hold_question: Should retrieval expose only the complete Obadiah 1:17-21 coda, or permit dependent Obadiah 1:17-18 and 1:19-21 children with mandatory 1:17-21 hydration?
hold_options: Expose only the complete Obadiah 1:17-21 coda, retaining 1:18|19 and 1:20|21 as internal seams.
Permit dependent Obadiah 1:17-18 and 1:19-21 children, both with mandatory Obadiah 1:17-21 hydration.

dissents.rationale: Literary review preserves three formal children but accepts the boss's larger-unit hold and bars standalone verse 21.
Canonical review preserves two dependent children as Option B; Hebrew review prefers whole-coda Option A without active appeal.
The renewed formula at verse 8 remains an internal alternative, but loss of understanding and wisdom/might collapse keep 1:5-9 coherent.
